content_of_post_to_answer: Why should we manage our self-esteem level?
answer: Self-esteem is often misunderstood as simply feeling good about yourself. A healthier view is that it is the internal measure you use to interpret failure, criticism, and success. Too little self-esteem makes every mistake feel like proof of inadequacy, while inflated self-esteem can prevent learning because it protects the ego from feedback. Managing it means keeping your self-worth stable while allowing your opinions, skills, and actions to be questioned. The goal is not to think highly of yourself all the time, but to stop letting every outcome decide your value.
